# splatmaker-mcp (full reference)

## Purpose

Self-hosted, zero-marginal-cost Gaussian-splat generation, wrapping one of several candidate FOSS engines (Postshot CLI, gsplat, Nerfstudio-derived pipelines - none chosen yet). Built as the cost-conscious alternative to worldlabs-mcp's Marble API for the same downstream chain: photo/video capture -> navigable 3D splat world -> blender-mcp finishing -> resonite-mcp / Resonite or VRChat world import.

## Status honesty

This is a v0.1.0 scaffold. What is real: the FastMCP 3.2+ server, dual transport (stdio for Claude Desktop/Cursor, streamable HTTP on /mcp for the webapp and fleet hub), the splat_generate portmanteau tool's full schema and job-tracking logic, the splat_engine_status introspection tool, the /api/health endpoint and mcp-federation-hub registration call per ORCHESTRATION_HIERARCHY.md's fleet contract, and a passing test suite (6 tests) that verifies the honest not_implemented behavior rather than a fake success path.

What is not yet real: the actual splat-generation engine. generate_from_video and generate_from_images will return status=not_implemented until an engine is chosen and its SplatBackend subclass is written in server.py. No SQLite persistence yet (jobs are in-memory, lost on restart). No webapp built yet (ports reserved: 11091 backend, 11092 frontend). No MCPB bundle. No glama.json health data beyond a stub.

## Tool reference

### splat_generate(operation, video_path=None, image_paths=None, job_id=None)

Portmanteau tool. operation is one of:
- from_video: start a job from a local video file path. Requires video_path. Returns {job_id, status, message}. status will be "not_implemented" until an engine is wired.
- from_images: start a job from a list of local image file paths. Requires image_paths. Same return shape as from_video.
- status: check a job's current status. Requires job_id. Returns {job_id, status, message}.
- list: list all known jobs (in-memory, this process's lifetime only). Returns {jobs: [{job_id, status, kind}, ...]}.
- get_asset: return the asset paths for a completed job. Requires job_id. Errors if the job is not in "done" status.

### splat_engine_status()

No arguments. Returns {engine, configured, note} describing which engine (if any) is set via the SPLATMAKER_ENGINE environment variable, and whether a real implementation exists for it (currently: no, for any value).

## Critical downstream integration note: no collision mesh

Unlike worldlabs-mcp, which returns assets.mesh.collider_mesh_url (a GLB collision mesh) alongside every generated splat, this server's output has no collision geometry. Any consumer - blender-mcp import, direct Resonite/VRChat world import - MUST route the raw splat through blender-mcp's blender_splatting tool (import, generate collision mesh, export) before the result is usable as a walkable VR space. Skipping this step produces a splat that looks correct in every screenshot and has no floor, walls, or furniture collision once someone is actually standing in it. This exact class of mistake was made once already in fleet documentation for worldlabs-mcp (in the opposite direction - assuming Blender needed to compute a collision mesh that worldlabs already provided) - see mcp-central-docs/architecture/FLEET_DEEP_ANALYSIS_2026-07-13.md section 2.2.1 for the full history. Do not repeat it here in the other direction.

## Fleet position

Registered in mcp-central-docs/operations/WEBAPP_PORTS.md (ports 11091/11092). Registers with mcp-federation-hub on HTTP-transport startup per the three-layer orchestration hierarchy (mcp-central-docs/architecture/ORCHESTRATION_HIERARCHY.md) - this server is a Layer 3 domain node, not a registry or a client of Fritz. Cataloged as a "medium" tier gestating chain (not yet promoted to a full build brief) in mcp-central-docs/projects/gestating-chains/medium-chains.md, which also carries the original Postshot/gsplat/Nerfstudio engine-choice discussion this scaffold deliberately did not resolve.

## Engine selection (researched 2026-07-13, not yet implemented)

Three candidates, compared 2026-07-13 (see README.md for the full table):
- Postshot: proprietary Windows desktop app (Jawset), GUI-first, no collider mesh export, CLI historically paywalled (currently free during a pricing restructure). ~2.5 years old, no public repo. Best hand-driven UX, worst fit for unattended subprocess dispatch.
- gsplat: Apache-2.0 Python/CUDA library, ~5.3k GitHub stars, no CLI at all (write your own training script), no mesh export, fastest raw training (~8 min on RTX 4090) and lowest VRAM (~4GB) of the three, but zero pipeline - SfM, export, everything is DIY glue code.
- Nerfstudio: Apache-2.0 Python framework built on gsplat, ~11.8k GitHub stars, real designed CLI (ns-process-data, ns-train, ns-export, ns-render), partial mesh export via ns-export tsdf/poisson (untested against its own Splatfacto gaussian method specifically), no fisheye/equirectangular/orthographic camera support.

Working recommendation, not yet acted on: Nerfstudio, on CLI fitness and Python-native fit with the fleet's uv-first tooling, not on raw speed. Load-bearing finding regardless of which wins: none of the three produce a collider mesh as a clean sidecar the way worldlabs-mcp does - blender-mcp's blender_splatting collision-mesh generation is a mandatory pipeline stage for any of these three, not an edge-case fallback.
